method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the Tot reduction, with exact formula, macro, label and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Undecidability of totality for indexed computable functions using the s-m-n theorem and K≤_m Tot.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Tot is the set of indices x such that φ_x(y) is defined for every y. The section uses s-m-n to prove that Tot is not computable.
samples.checks: The universal input quantifier, definedness condition, index-set meaning and noncomputability proposition remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: To reduce K to Tot, define partial h(x,y) to return zero for x in K and be undefined otherwise, independent of y. Simulate φ_x(x) and return zero only when it halts. The source expresses this as the constant-zero function composed with an unbounded search for T(x,x,s).
samples.checks: The K membership test, two case branches, ignored y, self-input x and µ-search formula are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The s-m-n theorem supplies primitive-recursive k(x) indexing the function of y that is constantly zero when x∈K and nowhere defined otherwise. Thus the function with index k(x) is total exactly for x∈K, making k a reduction from K to Tot.
samples.checks: Primitive-recursive strength, every-x-and-y quantification, zero and undefined cases, and reduction direction are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Tot is not even c.e.; it lies higher in the arithmetical hierarchy, but the stronger claim is not pursued here.
samples.checks: The non-c.e. strengthening, hierarchy placement and scope limitation are retained without importing an additional proof.
